title: LPV vs LNAV: The Minima Lines
hook: Four lines of minimums on one RNAV plate. Which one is yours?

scenes.narration: Thirty seconds. R NAV minima. One plate, a stack of lines — your equipment picks your line.
Top of the stack: L P V. WAAS gives you I L S-style guidance down to two hundred feet. No ground station, no towers — just math with a God complex.
L NAV V NAV: a D A with vertical guidance. Plain L NAV: step down to an M D A like it's nineteen seventy-five.
Check the annunciator by the final fix. Fly the line the box gives you, not the line you hoped for.
onScreenText: Check the annunciation by the FAF
Fly what the box gives you

scenes.narration: L P V like an I L S. Plain L NAV, dive-and-drive. Read the box's report card.
A I M one dash one dash eighteen. WAAS, explained by the hour.

quiz.question: Which RNAV minima line requires WAAS and provides ILS-like angular guidance?
quiz.explanation: LPV (Localizer Performance with Vertical guidance) uses WAAS for angular guidance and DAs as low as 200 ft. (AIM 1-1-18)

quiz.question: Flying to plain LNAV minimums, you descend to...
choices: An MDA — level off until the missed point or runway in sight
A DA — decide as you reach it
quiz.explanation: LNAV is lateral-only; its minimum is an MDA you must not descend below without the runway environment. (91.175)

quiz.question: Your GPS annunciates "LNAV" on an approach you briefed for LPV. You should:
choices: Ask ATC to fix your WAAS signal
quiz.explanation: The annunciated service level determines your line of minima — fly what the box is actually providing.
